SDV's TVAE architecture and mode-specific (BGMM) normalization scheme, plus CTGAN's conditional-GAN design, are adapted as the generative backbone of the authors' own crystal-generation pipeline rather than run unmodified from the library.

CTGAN is implemented using the CTGANSynthesizer class from the sdv library and, along with CopulaGAN (also from the SDV open-source library), is run as one of several baseline generators compared against the proposed CTTVAE+TBS model.

paper-ctabdm-conditional-tabular-diffusi.summary: This paper proposes CTabDM, a conditional tabular diffusion model that combines latent-space mapping with fault-type conditional constraints to generate synthetic minority-class dissolved gas analysis (DGA) samples for power transformer fault diagnosis, addressing severe class imbalance in this domain. The method is evaluated against Borderline-SMOTE, a CVAE-based generator, and CTGAN, using distribution-similarity metrics and downstream fault-diagnosis accuracy. CTGAN is described as a conditional GAN for tabular data and run as one of several deep generative baseline models compared against the proposed diffusion approach.

paper-fairfingan-fairness-aware-syntheti.summary: This paper proposes FairFinGAN, a WGAN-based framework for generating synthetic financial data that incorporates fairness constraints (statistical parity and equalized odds) via a classifier-based training objective, aiming to preserve fairness and utility simultaneously. The method is evaluated on five real-world financial datasets and compared against baseline GAN-based generators. CTGAN is run as one of the state-of-the-art baseline generators across all experiments, compared against TabFairGAN and the original data on fairness and predictive-performance metrics.

paper-amc-gan-iot-traffic-2026.summary: Observes that IoT flow attributes such as protocol, port, connection state and payload length carry the semantics distinguishing benign from malicious traffic, and that a discriminator judging samples globally lets the generator produce locally inconsistent rows, then proposes AMC-GAN, which quantile-transforms numeric features and groups features by correlation so those relationships are enforced during training. AMC-GAN is built on CTGAN: the paper describes it as the first CTGAN-based generative framework for IoT network traffic, keeps CTGAN's generator and discriminator pair and its conditional vector mechanism for encoded categorical attributes, and measures the result against a CTGAN baseline.

paper-generating-synthetic-tabular-large.summary: A survey/review paper that examines large and small language model (LLM/SLM)-based approaches for synthetic tabular data generation, such as GReaT and TabuLa, comparing their training strategies, conditioning mechanisms, and evaluation across downstream ML utility, data representativeness, and privacy preservation. The paper positions these transformer-based methods against earlier statistical and GAN-based generators discussed in prior literature. CTGAN is cited as a fast GAN-based baseline from earlier work, noted for its much shorter fine-tuning and sampling time compared to GReaT, but it is not run or re-implemented by the authors themselves.

paper-high-fidelity-synthetic-replicates.summary: This study uses a dual adversarial autoencoder to generate longitudinal synthetic electronic health records for nearly one million diabetic patients from the Andalusian Population Health Database, evaluating whether models trained on synthetic data can replicate clinical prediction performance (chronic kidney disease onset) while preserving statistical fidelity and patient privacy. The authors find synthetic-trained models match real-data performance and stable feature importance, but sex-stratified bias analysis reveals inconsistencies invisible to standard metrics. Fidelity metrics (e.g., Boundary/Category Adherence, KS Complement, correlation scores) and privacy risk metrics (disclosure protection scores, new row synthesis, membership inference AUROC) are computed using the SDMetrics Python package, while CTGAN is only cited in passing as one of the widely-used GAN-based tabular synthesis approaches, not run in the study.

paper-image-crash-severity-analysis-2026.summary: This paper proposes a framework that converts tabular barrier-crash data from Texas into image representations via the DeepInsight technique, then classifies severity using CNN architectures (Inception-ResNet-v2, Inception-v3, Xception) benchmarked against XGBoost. To address severe class imbalance in the crash dataset, the authors employ CTGAN to generate synthetic minority-class samples under under-sampling, over-sampling, and balanced sampling schemes before CNN training. CTGAN is run directly as the data-augmentation generator underpinning the entire class-balancing and downstream prediction pipeline.

paper-neural-network-copulas-generating-.summary: This paper proposes a neural network copula (NNC) framework that generates synthetic dichotomous item response data for cognitive ability assessments, decoupling marginal item modeling (via a deep autoencoder) from the dependence structure (via kernel density estimation) to preserve psychometric properties while protecting examinee privacy. The authors validate the framework against large-scale empirical IRT data, showing it reproduces score distributions, inter-item correlations, and item parameter estimates. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only as prior work on neural generative approaches to synthetic tabular/data generation and as an example of the distributional-divergence risk the authors' validation framework is designed to address; it is not implemented or run.

paper-neuro-fuzzy-modeling-decision-2026.summary: This paper builds a human-centered Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) to model and predict Counterfactual Decision Reflection outcomes in cyber defense exercises, using survey data on technical, emotional, motivational, and teamwork factors collected from a Lithuanian Armed Forces exercise. To address small, sparse behavioral datasets, the authors compare several synthetic data augmentation methods (SMOTE, ADASYN, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, Fuzzy Cluster, SMOTEBoost) and measure their effect on ANFIS predictive performance and distributional fidelity. CTGAN is run as one of several off-the-shelf synthetic data generators used to augment the training data, with its outputs benchmarked against SMOTE, ADASYN, and Gaussian Copula on consistency metrics and downstream model accuracy.

paper-physics-guided-deep-ensemble-2026.summary: This paper develops a physics-guided deep ensemble and inverse-design framework for low-carbon concrete mix design under data scarcity, combining a constrained tabular GAN for data augmentation, a heterogeneous ensemble (tree-based regressors, deep evidential regression, physics-regularized neural network) for slump/flow/strength prediction with uncertainty quantification, and an NSGA-III inverse design stage to find CO2-reducing mixes. To overcome a small 103-record dataset, the authors build a Physics-Informed/Regularized CTGAN (PI-CTGAN/PR-CTGAN) that extends CTGAN's generator loss with mass-balance, water-binder, and admixture-dosage constraints. CTGAN's generator loss function is directly modified into a new physics-constrained variant that produces the synthetic mixtures underlying the whole augmentation and modeling pipeline.

paper-posterior-calibrated-causal-circui.summary: This paper extends a mechanistic-interpretability framework for variational autoencoders (VAEs), originally built on image data, to four tabular benchmarks across five VAE architectures, introducing posterior-calibrated Causal Effect Strength, path-specific activation patching, and Feature-Group Disentanglement to test whether image-domain causal circuits generalize to heterogeneous tabular features. The authors find markedly lower circuit modularity and near-collapse of causal effect strength for beta-VAE on tabular data compared to images. In its background section on VAEs for tabular data, the paper cites Xu et al.'s work as showing that TVAE could generate synthetic tabular data with results comparable to or better than other approaches, but TVAE is not itself run or evaluated as one of the paper's own architectures.

paper-privfly-privacy-preserving-self-20.summary: Proposes PrivFly, a privacy-preserving intrusion detection framework for the Internet of Flying Things that combines self-supervised masked-feature reconstruction with differential privacy, and uses SHAP analysis to study the privacy-utility tradeoff on the ECU-IoFT dataset. To address severe class imbalance, the authors augment rare attack classes using either CTGAN or SMOTE, comparing the resulting detection performance under varying differential-privacy noise levels. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of two data augmentation methods for oversampling minority attack classes.

paper-tabrllm-tabular-generation-local-2.summary: This paper proposes TabRLLM, a low-data tabular generation method that uses an LLM to extract local-to-global integrity rules from feature groups and combines them with statistical distribution constraints to guide generation via prompts. It is evaluated on six real-world datasets against traditional deep generative baselines (CTGAN, TVAE, TabDDPM) and LLM-based methods, measuring downstream task performance, fidelity, and privacy. CTGAN and TVAE are run as baseline generators for comparison, and SDMetrics (attributed by the authors to the original SDV paper) is used to compute the fidelity metrics (RangeCoverage, CategoryCoverage, KSComplement, TVComplement, CorrelationSimilarity) that underpin the evaluation.

paper-trustworthy-digital-health-compreh.summary: This is a review article surveying methods for building trustworthy AI in digital health, organized around robustness and explainability across the AI lifecycle, with application domains including intensive care, mental health, and metabolic disease. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization approach is described in the survey's discussion of synthetic data generators for mitigating training bias, but it is not run by the authors.

paper-hybrid-physics-constrained-interpr.summary: This paper develops a hybrid physics-constrained interpretable machine learning framework for predicting the safety factor of natural gas hydrate-bearing submarine slopes, combining a gradient-penalized loss based on the 'φ = 0' undrained rule with a Whale Optimization Algorithm-optimized Support Vector Machine. The workflow follows 'physical generation → data augmentation → ML training → physical validation → interpretability analysis' to overcome scarcity of in-situ and simulation data. CTGAN is used in the data augmentation stage to synthesize additional tabular training samples that feed the downstream ML model.

The authors generate roughly 10,000 synthetic touch-feature samples per gesture direction, separately for genuine and impostor classes, to train and evaluate their classifiers. CTGAN, the conditional generative adversarial network for tabular data, is run as the generator producing the synthetic flick-gesture feature vectors that the whole authentication evaluation depends on.

SDV's library provides the foundation for the prototype, and its CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run as the primary evaluated generators driving the paper's core empirical results.

The two generators are assessed on fidelity to real data, privacy risk from record uniqueness, and utility for reproducing clinical analyses and training a postoperative outcome classifier. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run as one of two synthetic data generators whose outputs anchor the entire empirical comparison.

It benchmarks its generated signals against several generative baselines (CorGAN, medGAN, WGAN-GP, VAE, TTS-GAN, CTGAN) on time-domain similarity metrics and downstream diagnosis accuracy. CTGAN, described as constructing conditional vectors via a training-by-sampling strategy, is included as one of the comparison generators applied to sequential sensor data rather than its native tabular setting, suggesting the authors' own reimplementation of its conditional-vector mechanism rather than a run of the SDV package.

paper-snooker-dataset-generator-helpdesk.summary: This paper presents SNOOKER, a rule-based simulation framework that generates synthetic helpdesk ticket datasets, including cybersecurity incidents, by modeling IT teams, operator shifts, and ticket-handling workflows; its output is validated against a real anonymized dataset from S21Sec Cyber Solutions by Thales using distributional similarity tests. In its related-work survey of synthetic data generators, the paper describes the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) project as encompassing Copulas, CTGAN, and TGAN for statistical and deep-learning tabular data generation, and separately references SDV in discussing prior comparative studies of synthetic data generators. SDV, CTGAN and TGAN are only cited and characterized as existing tools; none are run in SNOOKER's own experiments.

It targets decision intelligence applications where real business time-series data is scarce or privacy-constrained. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in the reference list, with no textual engagement or use in the experiments.

paper-theseus-synthesis-privacy-preservi.summary: This paper proposes the Theseus Data Synthesis Approach (TDSA), a privacy-preserving synthetic data generation method that iteratively replaces partial records until no original record remains, aiming to balance cloud data sharing utility with personal privacy. It compares TDSA conceptually against other anonymization and synthesis techniques such as k-anonymity, differential privacy, and prior synthesizers, evaluating quality and utility of the resulting synthetic dataset. CTGAN is the population generator: it is trained on the person table and credited with generating tabular data and learning joint distributions, with its PacGAN discriminator preventing mode collapse, while activity locations are encoded as continuous rather than discrete variables specifically to stay within CTGAN's memory behaviour, and its inability to express hierarchical trip structure is the stated reason a separate recurrent model handles the trajectories.

paper-generative-models-synthetic-urban-.summary: A systematic literature review surveying more than 50 generative models proposed over the past decade for synthesizing urban human mobility data (trajectories, trip data, location sequences), comparing their privacy guarantees, architectures, and evaluation approaches, with a focus on practical applicability. In discussing gaps in the field, the authors cite the Synthetic Data Vault as an example of a standardized benchmarking tool offering shared datasets and evaluation metrics for tabular and time-series synthetic data, suggesting such tools could improve comparability across mobility-data models. SDV is mentioned only as an illustrative reference point, not run or evaluated in this review.

paper-gan-network-traffic-features-2023.summary: Generates synthetic network traffic features to relieve the shortage of labelled traffic data for security models, reproducing both categorical and continuous features and reporting how faithfully each architecture recovers the originals. Two of SDV's synthesizers are what the paper implements: CTGAN and CopulaGAN, run with SDV's reversible data transformation hyper transformer and its Gaussian copula transformer, and the paper sets out CTGAN's conditional architecture and mode-specific normalization as the design it builds the implementation on.

paper-leveraging-adversarial-samples-enh.summary: This paper proposes three machine-learning-based systems for detecting malicious and evasive PDF files, training models on both real and synthetically generated evasive samples to improve robustness against evasion attacks. The authors generate a 500,000-sample evasive dataset by training a Tabular Variational AutoEncoder (TVAE) on misclassified samples, explicitly relying on the SDV library (with embedding_dim=256 for 500 epochs) to produce this data. SDV's TVAE synthesizer is run directly as the generator producing the evasive training/testing data that the entire robustness evaluation depends on.

paper-meg-masked-ensemble-tabular-2023.summary: This paper proposes MEG, a Masked Ensemble Tabular Generator that uses a collection of Bayesian networks with masking operations and a group-based similarity measure to generate tabular data without requiring class labels, addressing a key limitation of the state-of-the-art GANBLR model. MEG is evaluated for machine-learning utility, statistical similarity, clustering applicability, and privacy robustness against baselines including GANBLR, TableGAN, and CtabGAN. CTGAN and TVAE, described via their mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling mechanisms, are run as unsupervised comparison baselines that MEG is shown to outperform.

Four SDV synthesizers, Gaussian Copula, CTGAN, CopulaGAN and TVAE, are evaluated on sleep data, making the paper a comparison within SDV's own model family rather than against outside alternatives.

paper-tabular-latent-space-synthetic-202.summary: A survey and unified taxonomy of 70 tabular and latent-space synthetic data generation algorithms across six machine-learning problems (anonymization, differential privacy, oversampling, data augmentation, active learning, and semi/self-supervised learning), classifying each by architecture, data space and scope, and reviewing quality metrics. It is a literature review rather than an experimental study, so no generator is run by the authors; SDV's Gaussian-copula anonymization approach, its CTGAN/TVAE extension, and its sequential (PAR-style) extension are described and placed within the taxonomy, and CTGAN/TVAE are cited as the source of mode-specific normalization and the conditional GAN design used by descendant methods (DPCTGAN, K-means CTGAN).

paper-dynamic-weighted-tabular-method-20.summary: This paper proposes DWTM, a feature-embedding technique that converts tabular data points into images by dynamically assigning canvas space to features based on their statistical correlation to class labels, then classifies them using CNN architectures (ResNet-18, DenseNet, InceptionV1). It positions DWTM against prior tabular-to-image methods like SuperTML and DeepInsight, achieving high accuracy across six benchmark datasets. CTGAN is mentioned only in related work, described as introducing mode-specific normalization and a conditional generator for modeling tabular data, but it is not implemented or run in the experiments.

The tutorial's outline lists GAN-based and autoregressive architectures for generating synthetic network traffic, including DoppleGANger, WP-GAN, ODDS, STAN, and CT-GAN/TVAE. paper-privacy-preserving-anomaly-detecti.summary: This paper evaluates the utility of synthetic data for anomaly detection (fraud detection) under supervised, semi-supervised and unsupervised settings, comparing models trained on real data against those trained on data from three synthesizers. paper-synthesising-tabular-datasets-wass.summary: This paper proposes WCGAN-GP, a Wasserstein Conditional GAN with gradient penalty for generating synthetic tabular mixed-type data, evaluated on three labelled real-world datasets against SMOTE for class preservation and data-protection metrics. preprint-does-what-says-tin-2026.summary: This paper proposes a method for creating synthetic data from categorical margins that have been curated and coarsened for statistical disclosure control, then reconstructed via Iterative Proportional Fitting to guarantee both transparency about preserved relationships and freedom from disclosure risk, illustrated on 1901 Scottish Census data. preprint-ipo-kendall-constrained-importa.summary: This paper proposes K-IPO, a generator-agnostic 'generate-then-select' oversampling framework that accepts synthetic minority-class candidates only if they preserve the original data's feature importance ranking (via a Kendall's tau constraint), evaluated across 20 imbalanced tabular datasets against several deep generative and classical oversamplers. CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula are run as the underlying generators/comparison baselines alongside SMOTE and TabDDPM to test whether K-IPO's acceptance mechanism can be layered on top of them and whether they distort feature-importance rankings. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and Gaussian Copula synthesizers are each run as evaluation subjects/baseline generators, one of several methods compared against the proposed K-IPO framework.

preprint-posterior-calibrated-causal-cir.summary: This paper extends a mechanistic-interpretability, causal-intervention framework from image VAEs to tabular VAEs, introducing posterior-calibrated Causal Effect Strength, path-specific activation patching, and Feature-Group Disentanglement, and finds that tabular VAE circuits are far less modular and more fragile than image-domain ones. preprint-privacy-preserving-machine-lear.summary: A survey providing a structured, cross-paradigm taxonomy of privacy-preserving machine learning for IoT, covering differential privacy, federated learning, homomorphic encryption/SMPC, and GAN-based generative synthesis, with analysis of privacy guarantees, overheads, scalability, and attack resilience across paradigms. paper-semapop-population-synthesis-2026.summary: Conditions population synthesis on semantics rather than leaving it unconditional: persona descriptions are written from survey records by a language model, encoded into a semantic space, and used as the conditioning signal for generation, which lets a planner steer the synthetic population toward a scenario instead of only reproducing the observed marginals. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the compared generators, set against Bayesian networks, a copula-based Bayesian network, TabDDPM and WGAN-GP on precision, recall and F1 over attribute combinations.

preprint-validation-stage-combinatorial-.summary: This paper studies Combinatorial Fusion Analysis (CFA), a rank-score model-subset selection framework, as a validation-stage method for improving fraud detection on the IEEE-CIS Kaggle benchmark, showing small but reliable gains over the best single gradient-boosted model. Separately, it runs a CTGAN augmentation experiment, training CTGAN on the training-set fraud samples to generate synthetic minority rows for class-balancing, and finds this augmentation degrades both individual classifiers and CFA performance. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run directly as a data-augmentation generator and rejected as unhelpful in this setting.

preprint-breaking-distortion-free-waterm.summary: This paper studies adversarial reverse-engineering of distortion-free LLM watermarking schemes, proposing an adaptive prompting and sorting-based algorithm to recover the hidden watermark key and mount spoofing attacks against watermarked LLMs like LLAMA-3.1-8B-Instruct and Mistral-7B-Instruct. The empirical work is entirely on LLM watermarking and text generation, unrelated to tabular data synthesis. CTGAN is cited only in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text.

preprint-doubling-your-minutes-ultra-202.summary: This preprint proposes SPADA, a lightweight tabular data generator that uses an LLM to induce a sparse dependency graph over features and then synthesizes values by traversing that graph with either kernel density estimation or a conditional normalizing flow, aiming to reduce constraint violations and sampling cost compared to LLM-based and diffusion-based generators. Experiments on four tabular datasets compare SPADA's fidelity, privacy (DCR), and speed against TVAE, CTGAN, GReaT, and TabSyn. CTGAN and TVAE are run unmodified as baseline generators in these benchmarks, with SPADA also cited via Patki et al. (2016) for its feature-typing taxonomy.

preprint-position-foundation-models-tabu.summary: This position paper argues that foundation models for tabular data are limited when isolated from operational context, and proposes Semantically Linked Tables (SLT) and Foundation Models for SLT (FMSLT) as a new model class that grounds tabular data in declarative, procedural, and world knowledge. preprint-privacy-auditing-synthetic-rele.summary: This paper proposes Gen-LRA, a computationally efficient No-Box membership inference attack that audits privacy leakage from synthetic tabular data by exploiting local overfitting via a localized likelihood-ratio statistic estimated with Gaussian KDEs. The authors provide a theoretical framework proving a mean-score gap between members and non-members, and benchmark Gen-LRA against several existing MIAs across nine tabular generative model architectures on OpenML datasets. CTGAN is one of these nine generator architectures evaluated as an attack target, run via the Synthcity package's implementation rather than the SDV library directly, with its mode-specific normalization technique described.

preprint-privacy-aware-time-series-2025.summary: Proposes Pub2Priv, a diffusion-based framework for generating privacy-aware time series by conditioning on heterogeneous public contextual metadata, using self-attention to encode public data into embeddings that guide a diffusion model, evaluated on finance, energy, and commodity trading domains. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing in the related-work discussion as an example of a conditional generator for tabular data, with no experiments run using it. preprint-tcdiff-triplex-cascaded-diffusi.summary: This paper proposes TCDiff, a triplex cascaded diffusion framework for generating high-fidelity multimodal electronic health records (continuous, discrete, and textual modalities) under incomplete clinical data, introducing a new benchmark dataset (TCM-SZ1) for Traditional Chinese Medicine EHRs. It reports that TCDiff outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by an average of 10% in data fidelity across various missing-data rates. CTGAN is cited in passing as an earlier GAN-based approach to structured medical data synthesis whose statistical integrity is compromised, but it is not implemented or benchmarked in the experiments.

preprint-pqmass-probabilistic-assessment.summary: This paper proposes PQMass, a likelihood-free, statistically rigorous method for comparing two sample sets to assess generative-model quality, using chi-squared tests over a partition of the sample space to yield a p-value without training auxiliary models. The authors demonstrate PQMass across several data modalities including images, simulation-based inference outputs, and tabular data. For the tabular-data experiment, CTGAN is trained on the Adult Census Dataset as the generative model whose synthetic samples are evaluated with PQMass, serving as the sole generator in that demonstration rather than a proposed contribution of the paper.

preprint-continuous-diffusion-mixed-type.summary: This paper proposes CDTD, a continuous diffusion model for mixed-type tabular data that unifies noise processes for continuous and categorical features via score matching and score interpolation, with adaptive feature- or type-specific noise schedules. preprint-designing-explainable-predictiv.summary: This work develops a design-science methodology for building prediction-oriented machine learning artifacts whose outputs can be explained to human decision-makers, and demonstrates it on an Airbnb price-prediction case study combining predictive analytics with explainable AI techniques. Both are cited purely bibliographically and never run or discussed further in the paper.

preprint-generating-tabular-datasets-dif.summary: This preprint (an MSc thesis-style work) proposes TableDiffusion, the first differentially-private diffusion model for tabular data synthesis, and benchmarks it against several DP GAN baselines including CTGAN, DP-WGAN, DP-auto-GAN and PATE-GAN across privacy budgets. The authors reimplement CTGAN's residual-network generator architecture and its mode-specific normalization/conditional sampling design as an unprivatised baseline used throughout the results, and separately adapt KS-distance and inverted-chi-squared metric implementations from the Synthetic Data Vault Project for their evaluation suite. CTGAN's architecture and conditional-vector design are reimplemented as a comparison baseline central to the whole benchmarking programme, while SDV's marginal-distance metrics are borrowed for evaluation.

preprint-bayesboost-identifying-handling.summary: This paper presents BayesBoost, a method that uses Bayesian networks to identify hard-to-predict data samples in ground-truth healthcare datasets and boost their representation when generating synthetic data, aiming to reduce under-representation bias carried into synthetic patient data. The generative approach itself is built on Bayesian networks rather than SDV models, and experiments evaluate predictive performance on synthetic samples produced this way. CTGAN, the conditional GAN for tabular data described in the SDV-family CTGAN paper, is run as the generator that produces all the concept-example data underlying the paper's experiments.

repo-time-series-analysis-with-spark.summary: Companion code for a Packt title on time-series analysis with Spark, one directory per chapter. Chapter eight generates its working series with `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` and `SingleTableMetadata`, so SDV supplies the data the chapter's analysis operates on.

repo-llama-cookbook.summary: Meta's official guide to building with Llama, covering inference, fine-tuning and RAG across end-to-end use cases. One of those use cases evaluates LLM-based evaluators on synthetic tabular data. SDV supplies that notebook's data: `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` and the demo-dataset loader are imported in `evals_with_synthetic_data.ipynb` to manufacture the benchmark tables the evaluator is scored on.
